name: Tunbridge Wells
description: Sell your broken supercar in Tunbridge Wells. Get a specialist assessment of engine, gearbox or electrical faults, with free collection once a sale is agreed.
hero: A major repair quote can change your plans for a supercar. Tell us about your faulty or non-running car in Tunbridge Wells and explore a sale with free collection by arrangement.
introTitle: Compare the repair option with an offer for the car as it stands
intro: A gearbox warning or engine fault can leave you deciding how much more time and money to put into a car. Before committing to further work, you can ask for a valuation based on its current condition. An offer depends on the complete vehicle and the information available about the problem.

We consider damaged and non-running Ferrari, Lamborghini, McLaren, Porsche and other specialist cars in Royal Tunbridge Wells. Include the model, mileage and history alongside a repair estimate. If the diagnosis is still uncertain, explain what has been checked and what remains a possibility.

Our team is based in Medway and arranges collection from agreed Tunbridge Wells locations. Tell us if the car is in a garage, at a specialist or on a drive where ground clearance could affect loading.
collectionTitle: Agree the access before agreeing the collection day
collectionIntro: Being able to start the engine and being able to load the car are different questions. Give us enough detail to plan both the sale and the recovery.

collection.title: Low ground clearance
collection.body: Explain whether a front splitter, lowered suspension or damaged underbody affects moving the car. Mention a sloping drive or sharp change of surface at the entrance.

collection.title: A vehicle awaiting diagnosis
collection.body: Tell us whether the workshop still needs access and when it can release the car. Share the current diagnosis rather than assuming an estimate guarantees the extent of the fault.

collection.title: A shared or private garage
collection.body: Confirm the person who can open the garage and make the route clear. If the car cannot select neutral or its wheels are locked, flag that before recovery is booked.

coverageIntro: We welcome enquiries in Royal Tunbridge Wells and the surrounding area. Nearby towns and villages are covered through the same agreed collection process.

areas.title: Royal Tunbridge Wells
areas.body: Town-centre and residential locations, including vehicles kept at a workshop or a private garage.

areas.title: Neighbouring locations
areas.body: Southborough and Rusthall, with other nearby addresses considered using the full collection postcode.

preparationTitle: Make a repair-versus-sale comparison with clear information

preparation.title: Understand the estimate
preparation.body: Keep the diagnosed fault separate from additional recommended work. Share any uncertainty or potential further investigation noted by the garage.

preparation.title: Describe the rest of the car
preparation.body: Record mileage, service history, specification and known body or interior damage. A fault is one part of the assessment, not the whole description.

preparation.title: Confirm what an offer assumes
preparation.body: Ask which condition details still need confirming. Accurate information about the vehicle and included parts helps avoid misunderstandings at collection.

closing: Send the details of your Tunbridge Wells supercar and any diagnosis you already have. We’ll discuss a possible sale and collection before you decide whether it suits your plans.

faqs.question: Can I get a valuation before approving a gearbox repair?
faqs.answer: Yes. Describe the gearbox symptoms or diagnosis, mileage and overall condition. A valuation for the car as it stands gives you an option to consider alongside the repair estimate.

faqs.question: Is Southborough covered as well as Tunbridge Wells?
faqs.answer: Yes. We welcome enquiries from Southborough, Rusthall and nearby locations. Give the full postcode where the car is kept so access and collection can be discussed.

faqs.question: Can you collect a very low car from a sloping drive?
faqs.answer: The approach and clearance need to be assessed first. Explain the gradient and any suspension or body damage. Photographs of the car and access can help establish a suitable plan.
